decisions.reason: The medical-association sense is explicit. Requesting a statement from its press office is coherent; the corrected Chinese no longer implies the journalist personally publishes the association’s statement. POS and selected meaning remain unchanged.

The supplied canonical is the masculine personal name; capitalization is the ordinary proper-name form. The new Chinese accurately preserves waiting until seats are found and removes the unsupported action 才继续. No real biography is claimed.

The surname sense is explicitly canonical. Lending the table and the purpose match; 售卖活动 correctly avoids adding charity/义卖, which the English sale does not establish. No geographic/person-name ambiguity remains in this selected sentence.

Ming is the explicitly stored dynasty name used attributively for the bowl. The corrected Chinese preserves case lighting and removes unexpressed porcelain material; the new pair does not invent the bowl’s substance or provenance.

The source contains the kiss noun; the count-noun pattern give someone a buss on the cheek is coherent. 匆匆吻了一下 conveys a brief/quick kiss rather than the prior unsupported gentleness; this is natural literary/old usage.

IBM explicitly confirms Systems Network Architecture and communications among network resources. A server exchanging data with terminals over an SNA network is coherent. Chinese now gives the architecture relation naturally, with no doubled architecture-network phrase.

The full canonical names reader/printer and the original Library Technology Reports item independently identifies a Minolta RP reader-printer in microfilming. The explicit parenthesis fixes the intended equipment reading; producing a print from a microfilm image is coherent, with faithful Chinese.

Collins explicitly confirms UNO as United Nations Organization. The selected name is canonical; calling on the organization to help mediate a dispute is an ordinary fictional request, not a claim that a particular intervention occurred. Chinese matches the request and help.

The source gives Latin medical adjective 大的. The attested anatomical name adductor magnus uses precisely that adjective; pointing out the actual muscle on a diagram is concrete use of the name rather than explaining where the string is placed. Chinese 大收肌 is accurate.
